title: How Red Bull Really Makes Money (14 Billion Cans a Year)
description:
Red Bull sold almost 14 billion cans in 2025 and its turnover passed €12 billion — yet partners fill most of the cans, and the company spends a fortune on Formula One, football clubs and a jump from the edge of space. In this file we open the money machine behind Red Bull: a Thai tonic drink and a jet-lagged toothpaste salesman, the $500,000 deal, why Red Bull behaves like a marketing company, the $1 Formula One team, the Stratos jump, where the money really comes from, who owns it, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Red Bull company profile (2025 figures); trend.at (Red Bull GmbH 2025 accounts and dividend); Vienna.AT and Bloomberg (2024 results); Fortune/Bloomberg (ownership); Guinness World Records (Stratos); Wikipedia (Red Bull, Dietrich Mateschitz, Chaleo Yoovidhya); tutor2u; Think Insights; Der Standard / The Economist.

All figures are rounded. Group turnover and cans are company figures; profit, margin and dividend figures are for the main Austrian company Red Bull GmbH, not the whole group. The ~90% energy-drink share of revenue, the 13% market share and the Yoovidhya dividend share are estimates or our own arithmetic. Caffeine content varies by country. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
